method: Exact unchanged renderer font sizes and 1920x1080 geometry; measurement only, not encoded-frame review.

lines: Open the intended day in Responder's Shifts workspace.
Here, Community standby signup is scheduled for Sunday, November
first, from eight until noon.
You are on confirms this account's current roster membership.
Read the notice that sign-ups and trades need supervisor
approval before changing coverage.
Request trade is available for this occurrence.
Verify the day and time first, especially when the same shift
name appears on several dates.
Choose Request trade
to open Request a trade.
The explanation says that everyone you pick is asked, and then
you choose from their offers.
Read the candidate names with their groups and roles.
Blake Gallo is shown with Truck eighty-one and Firefighter.
The other displayed candidates remain separate choices.
This is where you decide whom you intend to ask; a displayed name is not an
accepted offer or an approved replacement.
Select the checkbox for the intended person.
This exercise selects only Blake Gallo, and Selected, one confirms the count.
Enter a clear Note explaining the request.
Here, the note explicitly identifies a training exercise for
reviewing and cancelling a trade.
Review that note and the selected person before choosing Send request.
Confirm the colleague's suitability for your department's coverage needs as
part of the actual staffing decision.
Choose Send request once.
The returned day detail says, You have asked colleagues to take this shift,
and offers Cancel trade request.
You are on remains visible, along with the supervisor-approval rule.
These details establish the saved request state shown here.
They do not show an accepted offer, supervisor approval
or a completed handover.
Keep your department's actual coverage arrangements clear
while the request is outstanding.
Close the day sheet and choose Trades.
Under In progress, find the standby entry with the intended date and time.
It is marked Outgoing and Open, and includes the saved training Note.
Responses lists Blake Gallo with No reply yet.
Read the actual response label before planning a replacement.
In this recorded exercise, the colleague has not replied, and the request has not
produced an accepted coverage agreement.
Choose Cancel trade request on that outgoing entry.
The confirmation asks, Cancel this trade request, and repeats
the shift name, date and time.
Read the warning that any offers you have received will be discarded.
This example's preceding response state was No reply yet.
Verify the identity in the confirmation, then choose the red
Cancel trade request button to carry out the intended cancellation.
After confirmation, Trades shows No shift trades.
The earlier Open entry is no longer displayed in this queue.
A full page reload and a fresh visit to Trades return the same empty state.
This checks that the recorded result persists beyond the confirmation screen.
Read the application's actual returned state when doing this in your
department; this view does not present a separate cancellation-history record.
Choose Calendar to return to the day cards.
Find Sunday, November first, and compare the Community standby signup
card with the cancelled request.
Its eight-to-noon time range, You are on label and Approval
required label remain visible.
Open this matching card to recheck the saved day detail.
Using the full date and hours keeps a familiar shift name from being
confused with a different occurrence.
The reopened day detail identifies the same standby occurrence.
Request trade is available again, the outstanding-request notice is
absent, and You are on is retained.
Compare the date and time with the original request so you know
this is the same occurrence.
Cancelling the request has not demonstrated a replacement assignment.
This is still the signed-in person's recorded day membership.
Scroll through the same day's Roster.
Wallace Boden remains under Command with Chief and the Scheduled source label.
The Engine and Squad entries remain visible with their own people and roles.
This named readback helps you distinguish a cancelled request
from a transfer of responsibility.
Verify actual availability through your department's procedures before relying
on the roster for a real handover.
Use the same identity and result checks when community paramedicine or
mental health teams request outreach coverage, search-and-rescue teams
arrange support, security companies cover a post, wildland contractors
coordinate a crew, or industrial response teams plan standby staffing.
Fire and EMS departments can apply them to station coverage.
Keep a request, a colleague's response, required approval and the
final roster assignment distinct, and verify the actual result of each
operation your department performs.
